findings.evidence: NextProctorSessions captures from once with useState(() => new Date().toISOString()) and never advances it. The preview uses sessionStatus=SCHEDULED, direction=asc, page=0, size=3 and that same from on every query request/refetch/retry. StaffProfileSnapshot is kept mounted across tabs, so returning to Overview does not reconstruct this boundary. The server filters closesAt > filter.from, not closesAt > current request time. Both message catalogs promise up to three assigned scheduled sessions 'not yet ended'/ 'chưa hết giờ', including overdue openings.
findings.why_it_matters: A fresh preview request made later in the same mounted profile can still include a SCHEDULED session whose closing time has already passed, because it remains after the old mount-time lower bound. Older overdue sessions can occupy all three bounded slots and hide genuinely not-yet-ended assignments. This is a moving-time query freshness issue, not an objection to intentionally including overdue openings.
findings.required_action: Give the preview lower bound an explicit moving-time lifecycle: compute a fresh current Instant for each actual preview request or advance it at well-defined activation/refresh boundaries, keeping displayed 'not yet ended' semantics honest. Ensure retry and return-to-Overview cannot silently reuse the profile's original timestamp. Preserve bounded server filtering, include overdue-but-not-ended openings, retain tenant/target isolation and cancellation, and avoid per-render time keys that cause request/cache churn or client-filtering a bounded page as a substitute for server filtering.
findings.change_evidence: NextProctorSessions is a new untracked Phase05 source output, declared in the current phase Files; its frozen timestamp and moving-time copy are newly introduced.
findings.source_trace: Mount preview at T0 -> assigned session has opensAt < T0 < closesAt T1 and remains SCHEDULED -> later T2 > T1 return Overview or retry/refetch -> request still sends from=T0 -> server accepts closesAt=T1 > T0 -> response can display this elapsed session as not yet ended. Independent source trace only; no clock simulation/test/HTTP/browser execution.

resolution.evidence: New useNextStaffProctorSessions uses scope.key (staff detail prefix, authenticated tenant and target public ID) plus dedicated proctor-preview suffix. Its queryFn creates from=new Date().toISOString() at execution time and calls the existing abortable package request with SCHEDULED/asc/page0/STAFF_PREVIEW_PAGE_SIZE=3. No render-time timestamp in the key or mount-frozen from state remains. scope.ready && enabled gates inactive/unauthorized requests. NextProctorSessions consumes this hook; common Refresh and safe error Retry refetch the same hook and therefore recompute the time bound. Query invalidation/focus/activation fetch executions likewise use a current bound. The overlap predicate and overdue-but-not-ended interpretation remain unchanged.
resolution.conclusion: Moving-time preview request freshness and bounded/cache lifecycle are explicit. Source trace confirms the earlier mount-time lower-bound failure no longer applies. Static review only; no tests/browser/HTTP execution.

evaluation.server_filtering: Apply separates draft from applied query; apply/clear reset page; session/status/date filters and page/size are passed to dedicated staff endpoints. Local DataTable filter/sort/pagination are disabled. Page-local date grouping does not invent full-dataset totals. Existing tenant session catalog is option-only as explicitly required by phase, never used to derive workload counts.
evaluation.counts: All eight Proctor metrics are direct server fields, including separate ended/cancelled/awaiting-open/preparing/unscheduled. No attendance/completed-duty claim and no fabricated distinct exam identity. Dual-role examiner session count is separately labeled; Phase06 detailed grading metrics are not claimed implemented.
evaluation.preview: Bounded dedicated preview request now recomputes current Instant inside each fetch execution, with a stable tenant/target proctor-preview key and size3 constant. Includes overdue openings only while closesAt exceeds that request bound; this is not a promise every opensAt is future. Common Refresh and Retry use the same fresh-bound request path. QUAL-P05-001 resolved.
evaluation.timezone: Date utilities use explicit Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh UTC+7 bounds and next calendar-day exclusive end, not host/browser local timezone. Group labels and time cells use same display zone; null timestamps render unscheduled. Common timezone subtitle is visible. Shared server predicate excludes missing/invalid schedules with date filters.
evaluation.active_queries: Overview and preview are enabled only when Overview active; schedule queries/options only when Proctor active, gated by selected publicId and authenticated Host tenant. Role set controls work sections; public-ID keyed route resets target state. Reused tenant option query key avoids per-session fan-out.
evaluation.common_defaults: Uses stock CollapsibleSection/StatCard/Input/Select/Button/LoadingState/DataTable/PaginationControls/StatusBadge/ActionMenu without typography/color/trigger/sizing overrides. Feature composition changes layout only; no new dependencies/calendar/drag-and-drop.
evaluation.api_ownership: Package request owns optional AbortSignal compatibility; option/source hooks own transport through api-client and TanStack. Backend identity validates selected staff and requested role; server provides totals and dedicated projection. No personal Proctor console endpoint or mutation.
evaluation.navigation: Live Host app route /host/exams/[publicId] renders SessionDetailView with sessionPublicId; same-tab encoded session publicId route is correct. Existing Staff account query-error preservation/fail-closed behavior retained.
evaluation.error_loading: Common pending/error/retry/empty states distinguish failed requests from empty result; no raw API/internal errors are rendered. Main schedule paging disabled while fetching; no stale previous-filter rows are deliberately presented as new-filter data.
